To recap what actually happened,

Middle class premiums did not rise because of the ACA.  They rose because hospital monopolies, drug monopolies, and private insurers kept raising prices while Republicans sabotaged the law by cutting outreach, ending cost sharing payments, and blocking competition.  The ACA actually lowered uninsured rates, capped out of pocket costs, guaranteed coverage for preexisting conditions, and slowed spending growth compared to before 2010.

The so called free market will not work in health care because in many regions there is little to no competition.  People are not going to travel hours away for routine or emergency care, so the nearest hospital system becomes a de facto monopoly.  When hospitals are monopolies, insurance companies have no real leverage to negotiate prices, and costs keep rising no matter how much “choice” politicians talk about.

Your so called fix is not fixing anything.  Handing people a small cash amount does not control prices, does not stop monopolies, and does not create real choice when most areas have one hospital system and a few insurers.  It just shifts more risk and cost onto families while insurers and hospitals keep charging whatever they want.

If you want lower premiums, you regulate monopolies, negotiate drug prices, and give buyers real leverage.  Giving people crumbs and calling it freedom is not reform.
